decisions.reason: Report pinpoints plugin A's unconditional useSessionPendingInteraction call at client.js:219, explains alpha.2 dropped it in favor of useSessionStatus while useSessions remains, ties it to the single console TypeError, and shows plugin B uses no standard-kit hooks and throws nothing.

Grounds the damage in dock-render-tree.md: both dock entries are siblings under one DrawerErrorBoundary name="input.dock" with a null fallback, so A's throw unmounts B's chips; the attach button survives in input.left under a separate boundary, matching the console logs.

Reads the disable experiment as proving A's presence causes the unmount, explicitly lists what it does not prove (B's full alpha.2 compatibility, other dock defects), explains reinstalling B is pointless since B was never broken, and refutes the both-plugins-hit theory because B uses no standard-kit hooks.

Corrected code reads pending via useSessionStatus(...).pendingInteraction with a typeof function guard falling back to useSessionPendingInteraction then a stable empty map; only the pending highlight degrades while running/todos/token/ETA persist, and it explains silent degradation is required because a throw unmounts co-tenants under the shared boundary.

Verification needs only rebuild + refresh (no host restart), checks both entries mount together and B's paste flow as regression coverage with A enabled; hygiene recommends defensive destructuring, a local per-entry boundary, and discusses the host adding per-entry boundaries with the visibility/layout trade-off.

caps.reason: The final remedy fixes plugin A (the culprit) with graceful degradation; the report explicitly rejects reinstalling or fixing plugin B and asserts one crash with a shared-boundary blast radius, not two independent plugin bugs.
